item.title: Summer Live Music Series: Reggaddiction — Sat Jul 18, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Reggaddiction has been spreading the spirit of unity and community through their music since their formation in 2019. Fusing the timeless rhythms of Jamaican reggae with Canadian influences, Reggaddiction crafts a sound that not only transports listeners to sun-soaked tropical landscapes but also fosters a sense of togetherness and shared purpose. More than just a band, Reggaddiction embodies the ethos of ONE LOVE in everything they do. Their live performances are a powerful celebration of community, infused with the positive vibes of ska and reggae culture. Whether on stage or in the studio, Reggaddiction’s goal is to build connections, spark conversations, and inspire collective joy. They believe that music can unite people from all walks of life, creating a space where collaboration and oneness thrive.
Source: Distillery District

item.title: Dressing the Abbey Costume Exhibition — Sat Jul 18, 5:30 PM — Casa Loma
item.description:
Step into the world of Downton Abbey™ at Casa Loma with Dressing the Abbey, a special exhibition showcasing original costumes worn by the stars of the beloved television drama.
Featuring award-winning designs created by London costume house Cosprop Ltd., the exhibition highlights the elegance and evolution of British aristocratic fashion from the late Edwardian era through the 1920s. Guests can view everything from refined country tweeds and servants’ uniforms to lavish evening gowns adorned with intricate embroidery, lace, and beading.
Built in 1914, Casa Loma provides a fitting backdrop for the exhibition, with its grand Edwardian architecture and historic interiors offering an immersive setting that echoes the world of Downton Abbey™.
The exhibit is also included with a daytime GA ticket to Casa Loma.
Source: Toronto Events (Tockify)

item.description: Join us for Frequency — a monthly live music series at Worth Gallery. Frequency spotlights BIPOC musicians of varying genres through intimate, stripped-back shows. Celebrating sound, connection, and creative expression in Toronto's vibrant music scene. Find your new favorite musician in your new favorite gallery. This month's edition of Frequency features Shel Khan, an existential genre bending musician exploring different aspects of human life in her sound. Shel Khan is a Toronto-based musician blending alternative, grunge, soul, and industrial music. Her sound is fierce, vulnerable, and evocative, with songs exploring themes of ancestry, nature, consciousness, loss, human connection, existentialism, Buddhism, and dialectics. Human life contains soaring highs, bleak lows, beauty, violence, and everything in between. Shel aspires to touch as much of that multitude as possible. item.description:
Just in time for summer, Casa Loma is transforming the castle into Breathtaking Gardens, a new Sunday morning wellness series running June 7 through August 30, 2026.
Presented in partnership with Soul Expansion, the 13-week series invites guests to recharge through immersive live-music sessions led by Freddy Gervasi and The Band of Souls, along with local wellness instructors who guide yoga, Pilates, and somatic movement.
Set against Casa Loma’s lush summer gardens, the series offers a restorative start to the week in one of the city’s most iconic settings, with each session designed to calm the mind and support the body’s natural flow.

If you’re afraid of any of the big, loud, finger-severing tools downstairs this is your chance to learn to use them safely and make something practical at the same time. The goal of the class is to learn how to use common power tools and explore basic woodworking joints (mitre, rabbet, and dado). Your end goal is to create a lidded box with internal dimensions of 3″ x 3″ x 4″ that you’ll be able to cherish forever (or hide in shame, but hey, the point of the class is to learn the tools). We’ll start by learning how to use the planer and jointer to take a piece of rough lumber and turn it into a usable board. You’ll then use the table saw, chop saw, and router to shape those pieces, and finally the brad nailer, clamps, and glue to put it all together. If there’s enough time you’ll be able to sand down your creation, add some detailing with the router, and oil it.
